paper: Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil, Lee, Pang & Kleinberg (2012). Echoes of power: Language effects and power differences in social interaction. WWW 2012.
experiment: Independent reproduction of the Supreme Court results (Sections 3.2, 5.2, 5.3; Figures 4-5; Chief Justice contrast) on the public ConvoKit supreme-corpus 2004-2006 term files, using the existing regesh.bonding.synchrony measure with an authored non-LIWC lexicon. Directions and significance are comparable with the paper; absolute coordination levels are not.

data.name: ConvoKit supreme-corpus (term files 2004, 2005, 2006)
data.license_note: Public ConvoKit distribution of public-domain oral-argument transcripts (Oyez) with SCDB votes; not redistributed here. No utterance text is written to results.

cases.jsonl.used: cross-check of votes_side and advocate sides against conversations.json only

scdb_vote_info.tsv.note: present in the cache and checksummed; favorability comes from conversation meta votes_side, so the SCDB table is not read

case_set_source.file_commit: not obtainable: GitHub API access to CornellNLP/ConvoKit is disabled in this session; the master HEAD above pins the fetched content
case_set_source.notebook_warning: The notebook states that its code and data are not identical with the ones originally used in the paper.
case_set_source.convokit_code_role: read only to determine the threshold and aggregation semantics; ConvoKit is not installed or executed

case_id_filter: a conversation (argument session) is selected when its meta case_id without the 'YYYY_' prefix is in the alias-resolved set; the notebook filters utterances by u.meta['case_id'][5:] in case_ids without aliases (run as the sensitivity exact_notebook_case_ids)
entity: (speaker id, case id), following footnote 14; several argument sessions of one case share one entity
exchange: u2 with u2.reply_to == u1.id in the same conversation; distinct speakers; both texts non-empty; both speaker types in {J, A} (speakers.json type); speaker types differ (J->J and A->A replies are not status exchanges and are excluded)

speaker_types.A: advocate: lawyer or amicus, counted as lawyer for status analyses as in Section 3.2

chief_justice_note: Rehnquist was Chief Justice through the 2004 term (died 3 September 2005); Roberts from 29 September 2005 (2005 and 2006 terms). The run records in which term files each id appears.
lexicon: regesh.bonding.synchrony.LEXICON: authored open English function-word list; NOT the LIWC dictionary (451 lexemes) used by the paper. Absolute coordination levels are therefore not comparable with Figures 4-5; directions and significance are compared.

primary.name: convokit_wikipedia_example_7_7
primary.semantics: ConvoKit Coordination._scores_over_utterances: C^m(b, A) is defined only when at least target_thresh utterances of the targets in S_{A,b} exhibit m and at least speaker_thresh replies of b exhibit m. These are counts of marker-exhibiting utterances, pooled over the target group, not plain utterance counts. Values 7/7 are the notebook's Wikipedia example; the paper does not state thresholds.

notebook_supreme_3_3.note: the notebook's Supreme Court Figure 5(a) call uses target_thresh=3, speaker_thresh=3; its Figure 5(b) call uses target_thresh=6 with default speaker_thresh=0

eq1_only_min_7_exchanges.note: plain Eq. (1): defined whenever the target exhibits m at least once, entity needs at least 7 exchanges

favorability.lawyer_side: conversation meta advocates[speaker]['side']: 0 respondent, 1 petitioner; 2 amicus (supported side not recorded) and 3 unknown -> undefined
favorability.justice_side: conversation meta votes_side[justice]: 1 voted for petitioner, 0 for respondent; -1 unknown -> undefined
favorability.rule: favorable iff lawyer side == justice vote; exchanges with an undefined side are excluded from F5 (the notebook's selectors treat any inequality, including -1, as unfavorable; no -1 occurs in the selected sessions)
favorability.unit_primary: entity level: a lawyer entity toward the favorable or the unfavorable subset of Justices in its case (Eq. 2 over the filtered exchange set), and a Justice entity toward the lawyers it is favorable or unfavorable to; this mirrors the notebook's target_utterance_selector / speaker_utterance_selector
favorability.unit_sensitivity: pair level: (speaker, target, case) pairs; motivated by the Figure 5 legend counts (913 and 888 entities exceed the 535 lawyer entities of Figure 4), so the paper's unit for Figure 5 is ambiguous

statistics.primary: Welch two-sample t-test across entities, two-sided, hypothesised direction higher - lower
secondary: Student's independent t-test (the paper's caption says 'independent t-test')
paired t-test on entities present in both groups (fine status, F5a, F5b)
bootstrap percentile 95% interval of the difference of group means, resampling entities independently within each group
statistics.p_value_engine: scipy.stats.t when importable, else a normal approximation; the engine used is recorded in summary.json
statistics.multiplicity: none, matching the paper's uncorrected per-marker stars; the number of significant markers is reported descriptively

scale: coordination reported as percent (x100) as in the paper's figures

F4_lawyers_coordinate_more_than_justices.text: significantly more coordination from lawyers to Justices than vice versa (Figure 4)

fine_status_chief_over_associates.text: lawyers coordinate significantly more toward the Chief Justice than toward the Associate Justices (p<0.01); aggregate not specified

F5a_lawyers_to_unfavorable_over_favorabl.text: lawyers coordinate more toward unfavorable Justices than toward favorable Justices (Figure 5a)

F5b_favorable_justices_over_unfavorable.text: unfavorable Justices coordinate less toward lawyers than favorable Justices do (Figure 5b)

published.star_legend: independent t-test: * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001; figure values are percentages and are not printed in the text

declared_ambiguities: Lexicon: the paper used eight LIWC categories (451 lexemes); regesh.bonding.synchrony.LEXICON is an authored open list. Absolute levels differ; only directions and significance are compared.

Case set: the notebook's 204 ids include five that do not match ConvoKit case ids literally ('128orig', '105original' are original-jurisdiction cases stored as 128-orig and 105-orig; '04-1170b', '04-1360b', '04-473b' are second argument sessions of cases already in the set). Primary uses the alias map above (204 sessions, 201 ConvoKit case ids); the literal notebook filter (199 case ids, 202 sessions) is a sensitivity.

Thresholds: the paper does not state minimum-data rules. Primary adopts ConvoKit's semantics with the notebook's Wikipedia values 7/7 (marker-exhibiting utterance counts, not plain utterance counts); the notebook's Supreme Court values (3/3) and a plain Eq. (1) rule with at least 7 exchanges are sensitivities.

Exchanges: immediate replies via reply_to within one session; unknown/inaudible speakers and same-type (J->J, A->A) replies are excluded. The paper's 50,389 exchanges may include such replies; counts are reported by type.
Entities: (speaker, case) per footnote 14; two sessions of one case are merged into one entity.
Amici and unknown-side advocates count as lawyers for status claims (Section 3.2) and have undefined favorability, so they do not enter F5.
Favorability unit for Figure 5 is not stated; entity level (as the notebook) is primary and the pair level is a sensitivity.
Test: the paper says independent t-test without a variance assumption; Welch is primary, Student's is reported, plus bootstrap intervals and paired sensitivities.
Chief Justice identity is taken from speaker ids per term, not from corpus metadata (which has none).
outputs: entities.jsonl.gz (per-entity sufficient statistics and coordination values; no utterance text)
